name: com.atlamint/tax-calculators
title: AtlaMint tax calculators
description: Take-home pay and income tax return estimates in 19 countries, every step with its official source

tools.name: net_salary_netherlands
tools.description: Gross-to-net salary in the Netherlands for 2026: income tax with the general and labour tax credits, optional 8% holiday allowance on top, the 30% ruling (with its salary norm and cap) and a pension contribution. Returns net per month and per year and the effective tax rate. Single employee below state pension age.

gross_annual.description: Gross annual salary in euros, without holiday allowance (e.g. 60000)

holiday_allowance_on_top.description: Add the 8% holiday allowance (vakantiegeld) on top of the gross salary. Default false.

thirty_percent_ruling.description: The employee has the 30% ruling. Default false.

pension_percent.description: Employee pension contribution as % of salary, 0-30. Default 0.

tools.name: box3_wealth_tax
tools.description: Box 3 tax on savings and investments in the Netherlands for 2026 (the notional-return system): the tax-free allowance, the notional return on savings, investments and debts, and the 36% tax. Optionally for fiscal partners (double allowance). With a country and property or savings abroad (an expat's home country), also the treaty relief: the property is exempt, tax withheld abroad is credited.

savings.description: Bank and savings balances on 1 January, euros

investments.description: Investments and other assets (shares, crypto, a second home) on 1 January, euros

debts.description: Debts in Box 3 on 1 January (not the mortgage on your own home), euros

fiscal_partner.description: Filing together with a fiscal partner (amounts are the couple's total). Default false.

country.description: For assets in another country (2-letter code, e.g. IN, GB, DE, PL): the country, for the treaty relief. Leave out when everything is in the Netherlands.

property_abroad.description: Value of a home or land in that country on 1 January (your share), euros. Not included in investments. Exempt from Dutch Box 3 under the treaty, but it still counts for spreading the tax-free allowance.

other_assets_abroad.description: Savings and investments in that country on 1 January, euros. Not included in savings or investments. Taxed here; tax withheld there is credited.

tax_withheld_abroad.description: Tax already withheld in that country on those other assets (interest, dividends) for the year, euros.

tools.name: minimum_wage_netherlands
tools.description: The Dutch statutory minimum wage (wettelijk minimumloon) from 1 July 2026: the hourly rate for an age (21 and older get the full adult rate), and for a number of hours a week the gross pay per month and per year with the 8% holiday allowance (vakantiegeld), what is left after income tax, and the healthcare allowance (zorgtoeslag) a single person could get. Single employee without the 30% ruling or a pension contribution.

age.description: Age of the employee. Default 21 (the full adult rate applies from 21).

tools.name: woz_objection_netherlands
tools.description: Checks whether objecting to a Dutch WOZ value (the municipal home valuation) is worth it: compares the WOZ value with comparable sales by price per m², and shows what a lower value saves a year in eigenwoningforfait (Box 1) and OZB property tax, and the 6-week objection deadline. Without comparable sales it still gives the yearly OZB and how objecting works. Objecting is free; the decision (WOZ-beschikking) says the value and the date.

woz_value.description: WOZ value on the decision, in euros

living_area_m2.description: Living area of the home in m² (needed to compare with sales)

comparables.description: Comparable homes sold around the valuation date (1 January of the year before the WOZ year): price and living area. Two or more make the comparison usable.

woz_year.description: The year on the WOZ decision. Default 2026.

decision_date.description: Date on the WOZ decision, YYYY-MM-DD, for the deadline (optional)

ozb_rate_pct.description: OZB owner rate of the municipality, % of the WOZ value (on the tax assessment). Default 0.1.

taxable_income.description: Box 1 taxable income, to work out the tax rate on the eigenwoningforfait. Default: the 37.56% rate.

tools.name: salary_country_comparison
tools.description: Compares take-home pay in the Netherlands (2026, optionally with holiday allowance and the 30% ruling) with a salary in India, the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, France, Greece, Spain, Romania, Bulgaria, China, Poland, Turkey, Morocco, Belgium, Italy or Indonesia, converted to euros. Income tax and employee social contributions for one standard situation per country (single, no children, a named city or region where local taxes differ), as described in each country note.

nl_gross_annual.description: Gross yearly salary offered in the Netherlands, in euros, without holiday allowance

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Supported: IN, US, GB, DE, FR, GR, ES, RO, BG, CN, PL, TR, MA, BE, IT, ID (16 countries total).

home_gross_annual.description: Gross yearly salary in that country, in its own currency

fx_per_eur.description: Exchange rate: 1 euro = this many units of the other currency. Default: an indicative rate; ignored for euro countries.

nl_holiday_allowance.description: The Dutch offer pays 8% holiday allowance on top. Default true.

nl_thirty_percent_ruling.description: The 30% ruling applies in the Netherlands. Default false.

tools.name: dba_false_self_employment_check
tools.description: Indicates whether a Dutch freelance (ZZP) assignment risks being treated as disguised employment (schijnzelfstandigheid) under the DBA rules the Belastingdienst enforces again since 2025: authority, integration in the organisation, personal work and pay, and acting as an entrepreneur. Answer each question yes, partly or no; at least 4. An indication only; the official check is the Belastingdienst Webmodule Beoordeling Arbeidsrelatie.

howWhenWhere.description: Does the client decide how, when and where the work is done?

sameInstructions.description: Does the freelancer get the same instructions as employees doing the same work?

setsHours.description: Does the client set the hours or days worked?

coreWork.description: Is the work part of the client's normal, ongoing business?

looksLikeStaff.description: Does the freelancer work like staff, with the client's email address, badge or a place in a team?

longAssignment.description: Has the assignment lasted more than a year, or does it have no clear end?

mustDoPersonally.description: Must the freelancer do the work personally, without being able to send a replacement?

paidForTime.description: Is the pay per hour or per month, whatever the result?

clientCarriesRisk.description: If something goes wrong, does the client carry the cost instead of the freelancer?

severalClients.description: Does the freelancer work for several clients, with no single client giving most of the income?

investsOwnMeans.description: Does the freelancer pay for their own tools, training, insurance and marketing?

setsOwnRate.description: Does the freelancer set and negotiate their own rate?

tools.name: job_offer_comparison
tools.description: Compares two or three Dutch job offers by what is left after income tax in 2026: base salary, 8% holiday allowance, the 30% ruling (with its salary norm), the employee pension contribution and a bonus. Returns net per year and per month for each and the difference.

label.description: Name of the offer, e.g. the company (optional)

gross_annual.description: Gross base salary per year in euros, without holiday allowance

holiday_allowance.description: 8% holiday allowance on top. Default true.

pension_pct.description: Employee pension contribution, % of base salary. Default 0.

bonus.description: Expected gross bonus per year in euros. Default 0.

tools.name: fiscal_partner_split_netherlands
tools.description: For Dutch fiscal partners (married, registered or chosen in the tax return): finds the split of the own-home result (eigenwoningforfait minus mortgage interest), the joint Box 3 income and shared deductions between the two partners that gives the lowest total income tax, and how much it saves against 50/50 and against putting everything with the higher earner. Partners may divide these freely in the tax return (aangifte).

partner_a_gross_annual.description: Partner A gross yearly salary in euros (holiday allowance included)

partner_b_gross_annual.description: Partner B gross yearly salary in euros (0 if no income)

partner_a_pension_annual.description: Partner A own pension contribution per year. Default 0.

partner_b_pension_annual.description: Partner B own pension contribution per year. Default 0.

partner_a_thirty_percent_ruling.description: Partner A has the 30% ruling. Default false.

partner_b_thirty_percent_ruling.description: Partner B has the 30% ruling. Default false.

woz_value.description: WOZ value of the shared own home. Default 0 (renting).

mortgage_interest_annual.description: Deductible mortgage interest per year. Default 0.

debts.description: Joint Box 3 debts on 1 January. Default 0.

shared_deductions.description: Shared personal deductions above the threshold (gifts, specific healthcare costs). Default 0.

tools.name: personal_loan_affordability
tools.description: Checks a personal loan or other consumer credit in the Netherlands against a conservative guideline: total credit repayments of at most about 15% of net monthly income. Returns the monthly instalment for the amount, rate and term, the room left, and whether it fits. A rule of thumb, not a lender decision; Dutch lenders use NIBUD/NVB tables and check BKR registration.

net_monthly_income.description: Net income per month in euros

existing_monthly_debt_payments.description: Other monthly credit repayments (car lease, other loans). Default 0.

tools.name: cross_border_salary_netherlands
tools.description: Salary between the Netherlands and Germany, Belgium, the United Kingdom, India, Poland or Romania under the tax treaty and EU social security rules. mode "move": the year someone moves to the Netherlands (2026): Dutch tax on the resident part, the home country's tax on the salary before the move (Germany with progression; India's 182-day test for its April-March year), whether the home country also taxes the Dutch salary, and social security when posted. mode "commute": someone living in one country and working for an employer in the other: the salary split by working days (Germany: up to 34 home-working days from 2026 do not shift the taxing right), which country relieves double tax and how, and which country's social security applies (25% rule, telework framework agreement). Each answer cites the treaty articles. Salary only; Belgian and Polish tax amounts are not calculated yet.

mode.description: move = the year of moving to the Netherlands; commute = living in one country, working in the other

country.description: The other country: DE, BE, GB, IN, PL or RO

move_date.description: move: first day living in the Netherlands, YYYY-MM-DD in 2026

nl_gross_annual.description: move: Dutch gross salary for a full year, euros, without holiday allowance

home_salary_before_move.description: move: salary earned in the home country in 2026 before the move, in its currency. Default 0.

fx_per_eur.description: move: 1 euro = this many units of the home currency (optional; ignored for euro countries)

posted.description: move: still employed and posted by the home employer. Default false.

holiday_allowance.description: move: 8% holiday allowance on the Dutch salary. Default true.

thirty_percent_ruling.description: move: 30% ruling on the Dutch salary. Default false.

lives_in.description: commute: where the person lives; the employer is in the other country. Default other (lives abroad, works for a Dutch employer).

gross_annual.description: commute: gross yearly salary in euros

working_days.description: commute: total working days in the year. Default 220.

days_in_residence.description: commute: working days worked in the country of residence, home working included. Default 0.

telework_request.description: commute: employer and employee jointly asked to apply the EU telework framework agreement. Default false.

tools.name: visa_salary_check
tools.description: Checks whether a salary meets the 2026 IND salary requirement for a Dutch highly skilled migrant (kennismigrant) permit or an EU Blue Card. Holiday allowance does not count; a 13th month counts only when paid monthly. Also checks the 30% ruling salary norm.

salary.description: Gross salary in euros, as in the offer

per.description: Whether salary is per year or per month. Default year.

includes_holiday_pay.description: The salary amount includes the 8% holiday allowance. Default false.

permit.description: hsm = highly skilled migrant, bluecard = EU Blue Card. Default hsm.

under_30.description: Applicant is under 30 on the day the application is filed. Default false.

recent_graduate.description: Graduated within the last 3 years or on an orientation-year permit (reduced norm). Default false.

thirteenth_month.description: A 13th month: none, paid as a lump sum (does not count), or paid in 12 monthly parts (counts). Default none.

tools.name: job_loss_planner
tools.description: For an employee whose Dutch contract ends: the statutory transition payment (transitievergoeding), unemployment benefit (WW) amount and duration under UWV rules, and for expats the highly skilled migrant / Blue Card search period end date and the last start date for a new job to keep the 30% ruling.

gross_monthly.description: Gross base salary per month in euros, without holiday allowance

employment_start.description: Start date at this employer, YYYY-MM-DD

employment_end.description: Last day of the contract, YYYY-MM-DD

work_history_start_year.description: First calendar year with 208+ paid hours in NL or the EU. Default: the employment start year.

four_of_five_years.description: Worked in at least 4 of the last 5 calendar years. Default true.

permit.description: none (EU citizen), hsm (highly skilled migrant) or bluecard. Default none.

permit_two_years.description: Has held the permit for 2 years or more when the job ends. Default false.

tools.name: dutch_tax_changes_2027
tools.description: Compares income tax on a gross salary in 2026 with the Belastingplan 2027 proposal (presented on Prinsjesdag 2026, a proposal until Parliament votes): brackets and tax credits, and the 30% ruling dropping to 27% unless it started before 2024.

gross_annual.description: Gross annual salary in euros, without holiday allowance

ruling_started_before_2024.description: The ruling started before 2024 (keeps 30% in 2027). Default false.

tools.name: transfer_tax_netherlands
tools.description: Overdrachtsbelasting in 2026 when buying a home in the Netherlands: 2% for a home you live in, 0% for first-time buyers aged 18-34 up to a €555,000 price, 8% for other homes.

own_home.description: The buyer will live in it as their main home. Default true.

first_time_starter_exemption.description: The buyer has never used the starters exemption. Default true.

tools.name: us_tax_for_americans_in_netherlands
tools.description: For a US citizen or green-card holder with a Dutch salary: Dutch tax, the creditable part (AOW/Anw premiums are not creditable under the US-Dutch totalization agreement), and the US tax for 2026 under the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion and under the Foreign Tax Credit, incl. the child tax credit and its refundable part.

gross_annual_eur.description: Dutch gross annual salary in euros, without holiday allowance

thirty_percent_ruling.description: Has the Dutch 30% ruling. Default false.

children.description: Qualifying children under 17 with an SSN. Default 0.

other_us_income_usd.description: Other US-taxed income, e.g. US dividends, in dollars. Default 0.

usd_per_eur.description: Exchange rate, dollars per euro. Default 1.13.

tools.name: income_tax_return_netherlands
tools.description: Estimates the whole 2026 Dutch income tax return: Box 1 salary tax with the tax credits and the 30% ruling, the own home (eigenwoningforfait and mortgage interest, with the best split between fiscal partners), Box 3 on savings and investments, and tax-treaty relief for real estate abroad (exempt in the Netherlands). With the payroll tax already withheld it says whether you get money back or have to pay.

gross_annual.description: Gross annual salary in euros, without holiday allowance

holiday_allowance_on_top.description: Add the 8% holiday allowance on top. Default true.

payroll_tax_withheld.description: Payroll tax (loonheffing) withheld in the year, from the annual statement (jaaropgaaf). Optional: without it no refund/payment is given.

partner_gross_annual.description: Fiscal partner's gross annual salary (filing together). Omit for a single filer.

partner_payroll_tax_withheld.description: Payroll tax withheld for the partner. Optional.

woz_value.description: WOZ value of the own home (main residence). Omit if renting.

mortgage_interest_annual.description: Mortgage interest paid in the year on the own home, euros

savings.description: Savings on 1 January (couple total if filing together)

investments.description: Investments and other assets on 1 January, INCLUDING the value of any property abroad

debts.description: Box 3 debts on 1 January (not the own-home mortgage)

foreign_property_value.description: Value of real estate abroad (already included in investments), for treaty relief

foreign_property_country.description: ISO country code of that property, e.g. IN, GB, US, ES. Default: other (the same relief applies without a treaty).

tools.name: freelancer_tax_netherlands
tools.description: Estimates 2026 Dutch income tax for a self-employed person (ZZP / eenmanszaak) from yearly revenue and business costs: profit, the self-employed deduction (1,225-hour criterion), starters deduction, SME profit exemption, tax credits, the separate income-related healthcare contribution (Zvw) and the income left after tax. Also shows the VAT charged on the revenue. Read-only calculation; it files nothing and is not tax advice.

revenue.description: Yearly revenue in euros, excluding VAT

business_costs.description: Deductible business costs a year, excluding VAT. Default 0.

meets_hours_criterion.description: Works at least 1,225 hours a year on the business. Default true.

starter.description: Qualifies for the starters deduction (new entrepreneur). Default false.

vat_rate.description: VAT rate charged in %: 21, 9 or 0. Default 21.

tools.name: mortgage_netherlands
tools.description: For buying a home in the Netherlands in 2026: an indicative maximum mortgage on income, the monthly annuity payment, the first-year mortgage interest deduction worked out with the real Box 1 calculation (eigenwoningforfait, the deduction capped at the second-bracket rate), net monthly cost and whether NHG (national mortgage guarantee) is possible.

gross_annual_income.description: Household gross annual income in euros (both partners together)

price.description: Purchase price of the home in euros

loan_amount.description: Mortgage amount. Default: the price (Dutch mortgages go up to 100% of the value).

interest_rate_percent.description: Yearly interest rate in %, e.g. 3.9. Default 4. Use a current quote when you have one.

other_monthly_debt.description: Other monthly debt payments (student loan, car loan). Default 0.

claimant_gross_income.description: Gross income of the partner who takes the interest deduction. Default: the household income.

tools.name: benefits_toeslagen_check
tools.description: Estimates which main Dutch household benefits are likely for 2026, from income, assets, rent and children's ages, with indicative yearly amounts. Read-only; it does not apply for anything, and the Belastingdienst decides eligibility. Covers healthcare allowance (zorgtoeslag), rent allowance (huurtoeslag), child benefit (kinderbijslag), child budget (kindgebonden budget), the conditions for childcare allowance (kinderopvangtoeslag), the working-parent tax credit (IACK) and exemption from municipal taxes (kwijtschelding).

partner_income.description: Partner's yearly gross income. Omit if you have no (benefits) partner.

assets.description: Household savings and investments on 1 January. Default 0.

housing.description: Rent, own home, or other (e.g. living with parents). Default rent.

monthly_rent.description: Basic monthly rent (kale huur, without service costs). Needed for rent allowance.

child_ages.description: Ages of children under 18 living with you, e.g. [2, 7]. Default none.

you_work.description: You have paid work. Default true.

partner_works.description: Partner has paid work. Default true.

uses_childcare.description: Uses registered daycare, a childminder or after-school care. Default false.

tools.name: box3_actual_return_estimate
tools.description: When the actual return on Box 3 assets was lower than the notional return, the Belastingdienst taxes the actual return instead (following the Supreme Court rulings). For one tax year from 2017 to 2026 this compares the notional Box 3 tax with the tax on the actual return (interest, dividends, rent and value changes minus interest paid), and estimates the difference that could be refunded and which procedure applies to that year. Read-only calculation; it submits nothing and is not tax advice.

fiscal_partner.description: Amounts are a fiscal-partner couple's total. Default false.

savings.description: Savings on 1 January of that year

other_assets.description: Investments and other assets on 1 January

dividends_and_rent.description: Dividends and net rental income received

value_change.description: End value minus start value of investments, corrected for purchases and sales (negative for a loss)

assessed_box3_tax.description: The Box 3 tax on the actual assessment, if known (more exact than the estimate)

tools.name: gross_salary_for_target_net
tools.description: Reverse salary calculation for salary negotiations in the Netherlands (2026): the gross annual and monthly salary needed to take home a given net amount, with or without holiday allowance and the 30% ruling.

target_net_monthly.description: Net pay wanted per month in euros (yearly net / 12, so including holiday allowance when that is on)

holiday_allowance_on_top.description: The salary gets 8% holiday allowance on top. Default true.

thirty_percent_ruling.description: Will have the 30% ruling. Default false.

tools.name: thirty_percent_ruling_timeline
tools.description: Net income year by year for an employee with the Dutch 30% ruling: 30%, then 27% from 2027 for rulings that started in 2024 or later, the salary norm, the end of the ruling after five years, and Box 3 on Dutch and foreign assets (partial non-resident status only for rulings that started before 2024).

start_year.description: Year the ruling started (January assumed), 2019-2026. Default 2025.

partial_non_resident.description: Chose partial non-resident status (only for rulings that started before 2024). Default false.

dutch_assets.description: Savings and investments in the Netherlands, euros. Default 0.

fiscal_partner.description: Has a fiscal partner (double Box 3 allowance). Default false.

tools.name: rent_vs_buy_netherlands
tools.description: Compares the net cost of renting and of buying a home in the Netherlands over a number of years: rent with yearly increases and the return on the down payment if it stays invested (after Box 3), against mortgage payments, maintenance, the mortgage interest deduction and the equity built up.

property_value.description: Price of the home to buy, euros

down_payment.description: Own money put in (also pays the buying costs), euros. Default 10% of the price.

interest_rate_percent.description: Mortgage interest rate, % a year. Default 3.9.

gross_income.description: Gross income of the person who deducts the mortgage interest, euros a year. Default 60000.

home_value_growth_percent.description: Yearly change in the home's value, %. Default 2.

maintenance_percent.description: Yearly maintenance and owners' association costs, % of the value. Default 1.

investment_return_percent.description: What the down payment would earn if invested instead, % a year. Default 4.

fiscal_partner.description: Filing with a fiscal partner. Default false.

tools.name: gift_tax_netherlands
tools.description: Gift tax in the Netherlands for 2026: the yearly exemption for children and others, the one-time raised exemption (general or for study) for a recipient aged 18-40, the rates per relationship and whether a gift tax return must be filed. The recipient pays; Dutch tax applies when the giver lives in the Netherlands.

amount.description: Total given by this giver this year (both parents count as one giver), euros

relationship.description: The recipient is the giver's child, grandchild, or anyone else

giver_lives_in_netherlands.description: The giver lives in the Netherlands. Default true.

recipient_aged_18_to_40.description: The recipient (or their partner) is 18-40 on the day of the gift. Default false.

one_time_exemption.description: Claim the one-time raised exemption. Default none.

tools.name: inheritance_tax_netherlands
tools.description: Inheritance tax in the Netherlands for 2026 for one heir: the exemption for a partner, child, disabled child, grandchild, parent or anyone else, and the rates of each group. Due when the deceased lived in the Netherlands.

amount.description: Value of this heir's share, euros

relationship.description: The heir's relationship to the deceased

deceased_lived_in_netherlands.description: The deceased lived in the Netherlands. Default true.

tools.name: company_car_tax_netherlands
tools.description: The yearly addition to income (bijtelling) for private use of a company car in the Netherlands in 2026, for electric and fuel cars (with the 60-month lock-in of an electric car's rate and cap from its first registration), and the extra income tax at the employee's marginal rate.

catalog_value.description: The car's list price (catalogue value incl. BPM and VAT), euros

taxable_income.description: Taxable income before the bijtelling, euros a year. Default 60000.

first_registration_year.description: Year the car was first registered (sets an electric car's rate for 60 months). Default 2026.

tools.name: pension_annuity_room_jaarruimte
tools.description: How much an employee or freelancer in the Netherlands may deposit into an annuity (lijfrente) or pension bank account in 2026 and deduct in Box 1: the jaarruimte from last year's income and factor A, unused room from earlier years (reserveringsruimte), and the tax the remaining room saves.

last_year_income.description: 2025 income from work or business, euros

factor_a.description: Factor A on the 2025 pension statement (UPO); 0 without an employer pension. Default 0.

already_paid.description: Annuity premiums already paid in 2026, euros. Default 0.

this_year_taxable_income.description: 2026 taxable Box 1 income, for the tax saving. Default the same as last year.

tools.name: employee_vs_zzp_vs_bv
tools.description: For one yearly budget (what a client or employer pays, excl. VAT) in the Netherlands in 2026: the net income as an employee (the budget covers salary and employer costs), as a freelancer (ZZP, with the entrepreneur deductions) and through your own BV (salary at least the customary wage, corporate tax and Box 2 on the dividend).

yearly_budget.description: Yearly amount the client or employer pays, excl. VAT, euros

business_costs.description: Yearly business costs as ZZP or BV, euros. Default 5000.

bv_extra_costs.description: Extra yearly cost of running a BV (accountant, annual accounts), euros. Default 3000.

bv_salary.description: Salary the BV pays you, euros a year. Default the customary wage (or less if the BV can't pay it).

meets_hours_criterion.description: At least 1,225 hours a year in the business (for the ZZP deductions). Default true.

tools.name: freelance_hourly_rate
tools.description: The hourly rate a freelancer (ZZP) in the Netherlands needs in 2026 to take home a target net amount a month, after holidays, sick days and hours that can't be invoiced, business costs, the entrepreneur deductions, income tax and the Zvw contribution.

target_net_monthly.description: Net income wanted a month, euros

holiday_weeks.description: Weeks off a year, incl. public holidays. Default 6.

non_billable_percent.description: Share of working hours not invoiced (sales, admin), %. Default 20.

business_costs.description: Yearly business costs excl. VAT, euros. Default 3000.

starter.description: Gets the starters deduction (one of the first five years). Default false.

tools.name: rsu_tax_netherlands
tools.description: Tax on restricted stock units in the Netherlands: each vest is taxed as wages in Box 1 at the value on the vesting day (with or without the 30% ruling), and shares you keep fall into Box 3 the next year. Year by year, with sell-to-cover or keeping the shares.

salary.description: Gross base salary a year, euros

grant_value.description: Value of the whole grant today, euros

vest_years.description: Years over which it vests evenly, 1-6. Default 4.

share_growth_percent.description: Expected share price change a year, %. Default 0.

keep_shares.description: Keep the net shares (true) or sell everything at vesting. Default false.

other_box3_assets.description: Other savings and investments, euros. Default 0.

tools.name: arrival_departure_year_m_form
tools.description: For the year someone arrives in or leaves the Netherlands (the M-form, migration tax return): the salary earned while resident, the Dutch tax on it with the tax credits for that part of the year, and the net pay a month during the resident period.

scenario.description: Moving to the Netherlands or leaving it

date.description: Registration date in the municipality (arriving) or departure date (leaving), YYYY-MM-DD, 2024-2026

gross_annual.description: Gross salary for a full year at this pay, euros

tools.name: marginal_rate_allowance_cliff
tools.description: For a salary in the Netherlands in 2026: the allowances a household gets (healthcare and rent allowance, child budget), the net income including them, and the share of the next €1,000 of salary that is kept after extra income tax and lost allowances. Also lists the salary ranges where a raise is mostly lost.

monthly_rent.description: Monthly rent for rent allowance, 0 if owning. Default 0.

children_ages.description: Ages of children under 18. Default none.

partner.description: Has an allowance partner. Default false.

partner_income.description: The partner's yearly income, euros. Default 0.

assets.description: Savings and investments on 1 January, euros. Default 0.

tools.name: health_insurance_cost_netherlands
tools.description: The yearly cost of basic health insurance in the Netherlands in 2026: premium (with the discount for a voluntary extra deductible), the deductible (eigen risico) actually paid for expected care costs, and the healthcare allowance (zorgtoeslag) for the income.

annual_income.description: Yearly income for the healthcare allowance, euros

monthly_premium.description: Basic insurance premium a month, euros. Default 160.

expected_care_costs.description: Expected care costs a year that fall under the deductible, euros. Default 0.

allowance_partner.description: Has an allowance partner. Default false.

tools.name: aow_state_pension
tools.description: The Dutch state pension (AOW) from 1 July 2026 for a single person or someone with a partner: 2% of the full AOW for every insured year in the Netherlands in the 50 years before AOW age, gross and net a month, and the holiday allowance.

tools.name: cross_border_year
tools.description: Estimates the employment income tax in BOTH countries for the tax year in which someone moves from one country to another: residency status in each country by its own rules (India's 182-day financial-year test, US substantial presence and dual-status, UK split year, Dutch migration year, German part-year liability), the income each country taxes, tax before and after relief for tax paid abroad, social contributions, the combined total in euros and a comparison with staying. Covers 19 countries; each country is taxed for its own tax year containing the move date. Returns what is not covered, assumptions, and for researched corridors (India with the Netherlands, US, UK or Germany; Netherlands with Germany or the UK) the forms and deadlines, treaty notes and official sources. Salaries are full-year rates in each country's own currency.
